newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains slow harvest of Brazil centre-south sugar.
newsitem.headline: Rains slow harvest of Brazil centre-south sugar.

text.p: Rains have slowed the harvest of Brazil's 1997/98 centre-south sugar cane crop in the last two weeks but it was still progressing at a slightly faster pace than last year, a sugar official said.

"Harvesting began earlier than usual this year but we have lost the advantage of that earlier start because of rain," Luis Carlos Correa Carvalho of the Sao Paulo Sugar Industry Union (Unica) told Reuters at a seminar on alcohol production.
By June 1, centre-south producers had harvested 27.139 million tonnes of sugar cane and produced 1.229 million tonnes of sugar, according to Unica figures.
The region produced 476,023 tonnes anhydrous alcohol and 1.254 million tonnes of hydrous alcohol.

Unica -- which replaces the Sao Paulo Sugar And Alcohol Industries Association (AIAA) previously responsible for publishing centre-south sugar statistics -- did not provide comparative figures for 1996/97.

But Carvalho said that statistics to May 15 showed harvesting was well ahead of the previous year, although he expected this effect to be more subdued in the figures to mid-June because of two weeks of rain.

"We have a lot of cane. Harvesting in May was quite sharply higher than the previous year and maybe we are still above last year's levels," said Carvalho, adding, "Probably the June 15 position will be a little more subdued."
The industry was preparing itself for the liberalization of the sugar and hydrous alcohol sector by the government's stated target date of May 1998, Carvalho said.
"There is an ever greater effort to reduce costs. The key of the process is to be competitive," he said.
But it was equally important for the government to help the sector by compensating for the advantage of petrol prices over alcohol, possibly by introducing an ecological tax on petrol, Carvalho said.
